messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: sudden tail-latency and KV cache size spike observed for hosted-prod (us-west1). Alert: kv_cache_key_count > 10M and continuous-batch queue depth rising rapidly. Paging oncall.

alex: Seeing a ton of promptcache entries with near-0 hit rate since 10:04 UTC. Latency p95 -> 1.8s from normal ~120ms. CPU on inference pods stable, but redis memory + IO skyrocketed.

alex: logs snippet:
```
[10:04:12] promptcache: miss key_count=10_243_112 hit_rate=0.03 prefix_version=v2.1.0-tokenizer_b
[10:05:01] batching: queue_size=8200 avg_batch_len=134 max_batch_len=512
[10:05:03] kv-write-errors: E_BUSY write_latency_ms=980
```

maya: I rolled tokenization v2.1.0 to us-west yesterday. It changed byte-level whitespace normalization and hash salt. wondering if promptkey generation changed.

chris: Confirmed correlation: rollout started 09:50 and cache miss spike ~10:02. Could be hashing/tokenizer mismatch invalidating prefixes which causes many new keys -> cache blowup and backend pressure.

becky: Support picking up customer hits: several 504s reported by Clearline (#5421) between 10:03-10:10. They're on us-west1. Escalating to SE.

sre-ops: Initial mitigations: 1) throttle continuous batching (set max_batch_len=64), 2) enable synchronous KV write backoff, 3) schedule promptcache scrub/sampler. Will attempt live rollback of tokenizer if needed.

maya: I'm running a quick config change to reduce batch size now.
```
# reduce continuous batch max
kubectl -n redwood set env deployment/infer-serving MAX_CONTINUOUS_BATCH=64 --record
```

alex: Doing a dry-run scrub to find high-entropy prefixes to evict (non-blocking):
```
redis-cli -h promptcache-prod --scan | grep 'prompt:' | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1000 redis-cli -h promptcache-prod del
# running controlled deletes in small batches
```

incident-bot: ACTIONS_LOGGED: throttle-batching applied, cache-scrub-started, support-ticket-tagged. Paging continues until ack.

chris: Acked. I'll take ownership for live mitigation and handoff. Starting full revert plan if scrub + throttle don't bring p95 under 400ms in next 10m.

support-bot: Noted customer impact: #5421 -> 3 users affected, 504s, severity P2. Notifying account team.

alex: Observed immediate drop in avg_batch_len from 134 -> 58 after throttle. CPU on serving nodes decreased, redis IO still elevated but trending down.

maya: Rollback plan: revert tokenizer to v2.0.7 in us-west1 can be done via rollout undo. Needs ~5m to complete and another few minutes for cache churn.

chris: Before rollback let's try controlled prefix key remap: generate legacy-prefixed keys for a small fraction of traffic to hit existing cache instead of full revert. If that fails, full rollback.

becky: Customer-facing note drafted for Clearline: "We're investigating increased latency and intermittent timeouts in US-WEST1; mitigation in progress." Waiting on timeline for rollback decision.

sre-ops: Within 8m of throttle + targeted scrub we saw p95 drop to 380ms and 200ms for p50. Cache size down ~40%. Recommend continue scrub + monitor for 15m before rollback.

alex: While we monitor, flag for postmortem: promptkey generation should be backwards-compatible; tokenization change must have altered prefix hashing salt or template trimming. Also batching heuristics shouldn't expand so much on cache miss storms.

chris: If we need to rollback, command:
```
redwoodctl rollout undo infer-tokenizer --namespace us-west1 --to-version v2.0.7
```
I'll coordinate with maya and infra during the operation window.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: chris is owning mitigation. next-oncall -> chris. Please ack within 5m.

chris: ack

support-bot: Update: Clearline ticket updated, SE notified, CS will follow up if we hit additional errors.

maya: scrub script result (summary): removed ~1.2M high-entropy keys (non-cold), reduced redis memory by ~18GB. No spike in 5xx during deletes.

alex: perf graph: p95 trending down, continuous-batch queue depth back to normal. Looks like scrub + throttle helped.

chris: We're leaving tokenizer v2.1.0 rolled out but with protections: batch_max=64, gradual key remap disabled, enable stricter prefix hashing compatibility flag. Need hotfix to make tokenizer emit stable prefix hash (compat mode).

sre-ops: Creating incident ticket and provisional RCA: root cause hypothesis -> tokenizer rollout changed normalization -> prefix_hash salt/format changed -> cache invalidation -> cache miss storm -> batching policy amplified request coalescing -> KV write amplification and IO saturation -> customer timeouts.

becky: Filing customer followup and collection of logs. SE will propose a credit for Clearline; will draft comms after final RCA.

chris: Next steps assigned:
- maya: implement tokenizer compat mode flag and test in staging
- alex: write a cache-safe rollout checklist and add automated key-compatibility test
- sre-ops: add automatic throttle when cache_miss_rate > 0.3 and queue_depth > 2000
- becky: coordinate customer comms

incident-bot: INCIDENT_STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owner assigned: alex. Timeline doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2468001234

sre-ops: leaving a note: we should add a chaos test that mutates tokenization and checks cache hit regressions before any tokenizer change hits prod.

chris: closing live paging. I'll hand back to oncall rotation update in #eng-oncall. Great work everyone :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #5421 updated. Marking customer impact as resolved pending follow-up.

alex: I'll start the postmortem draft now and include artifacts (redis memory graphs, rollout timeline, scrub logs, config diffs).
